claims.claim: OpenAI prompt caching depends on matching prefixes, including identical tool definitions and their ordering.
claims.application: Use deterministic compact schemas and output ordering. Measure total and cached input separately. Memglide cannot force a Codex provider cache hit.
claims.limits: The cookbook discusses the API and earlier model examples; advertised maximum speed/cost reductions are not Memglide measurements or guarantees for ChatGPT-authenticated Codex.

claims.claim: Fewer unnecessary sequential tool interactions and filtering results before model ingestion are established agent-design techniques.
claims.application: Prototype one server-side bootstrap for project resolution, session creation and initial retrieval; include compact freshness evidence in that result.
claims.limits: The Anthropic API feature is not a Codex configuration setting. A wrapper can add complexity and may not reduce underlying model calls or latency; only native usage/timing can establish that.

claims.claim: Deferred discovery can reduce initial schema exposure; Codex supports an explicit enabled_tools filter.
claims.application: Offer a stable compact tool profile with bootstrap and focused expansion, while preserving the full compatible profile for integrations.
claims.limits: Claude defer_loading and tool_reference are provider-specific and must not be passed to Codex as invented flags. Smaller serialized schema bytes are a proxy, not measured model tokens.

claims.claim: Repository-level code tasks can require cross-file context, while small retrieval chunks and larger returned parent context serve different purposes.
claims.application: Use precise identifier/path retrieval, then pack complete direct definitions and bounded direct helpers where possible; expose explicit truncation/omission markers and expansion.
claims.limits: The sources do not prove AST chunks or any particular dependency graph algorithm are best. RepoCoder uses line windows and does not guarantee complete functions. Direct-helper completeness is a local hypothesis to test.

claims.claim: The Lost-in-the-Middle experiment deliberately varies relevant-passage position among fixed distractors.
claims.application: Keep the most relevant unique source early; avoid burying it below metadata or large graph expansions. Consider fixed-content ordering ablations.
claims.limits: Only author experiment code/instructions were inspected here, not the full paper. No quantitative position effect is imported, and older QA-model findings are not proof about current Codex coding agents.

claims.claim: Memory, compaction and re-fetchable tool-result clearing address different context problems; memory can become stale and resource subscriptions are optional.
claims.application: Validate freshness with source identity/hash and mutation tests; keep model-needed markers visible. Test warm memory across related sessions separately from cold retrieval.
claims.limits: Memglide cannot edit Codex internal conversation history or activate Claude context-management API features. A server Current label alone is not an independent live-hash check.

claims.claim: Retrieval quality and final execution-based coding quality require separate evaluation, and high-quality context does not guarantee a gain for every model/task.
claims.application: Keep reference-file/body coverage, precision and ranking diagnostics separate from hidden behavioral task success, actual usage and elapsed time.
claims.limits: No source establishes that Memglide saves tokens, money or time. A larger embedding/reranker stack can cost more CPU, memory and latency than it returns on small tasks.

claims.claim: A credible coding grader checks both the requested behavior and preservation of existing passing behavior, including evidence that tests really ran.
claims.application: Use independent hidden behavioral graders, unchanged smoke checks and compilation; detect protected-file edits and empty/nonexecuted suites. Preserve all failures and interrupted attempts.
claims.limits: Passing the selected tests does not prove arbitrary correctness. Local synthetic tasks, repeats and mirrored languages are correlated.

claims.claim: For direct tool output in Codex 0.159.2, text JSON plus non-null structuredContent is not automatically duplicated in the model context: structuredContent is selected and serialized once.
claims.application: Retain the compatible structured-result contract by default. Do not claim a 50% token saving merely by deleting one SDK envelope representation.
claims.limits: MCP events and transport storage can still contain both. Envelope byte size is not model token usage; encrypted content has a different conversion branch.

claims.claim: Code Mode receives the full result envelope minus _meta, then exposes only emitted runtime content to the model.
claims.application: Keep freshness/completeness data in visible structured/text fields. Test whether an optional compact result profile or selecting structuredContent avoids repeated payloads.
claims.limits: Duplication reaches the model only if the generated JavaScript emits both representations/the whole envelope. Native MCP JSONL alone does not show that choice. Actual CLI usage must validate any token reduction.

candidate_experiments.mechanism: Resolve project, start/reuse session and retrieve in one server-side operation; retain focused expansion.
checks: Verify native B invocation and delivered source, not only process startup.
Compare MCP call counts and actual CLI input/cached/output tokens plus elapsed time.
Keep same model, effort, prompts and independent graders; declare the integration change.
candidate_experiments.tradeoff: A combined tool can hide errors or create state unexpectedly; preserve isolation, clear failures and compatibility.

candidate_experiments.mechanism: Remove repeated graph/debug metadata, duplicate spans and unchanged context while preserving paths, ranges, version/freshness, omissions and complete useful definitions.
checks: Compare full-body and direct-helper coverage, precision, explicit truncation and actual structured results.
Measure serialized bytes only as bytes; use native usage for model token conclusions.
Do not silently omit stale/partial warnings.
candidate_experiments.tradeoff: Aggressive compression can remove necessary code or make errors harder to diagnose; provide explicit expansion.

candidate_experiments.mechanism: Carry source/index identity in compact results and reject/rebuild stale evidence on edits, renames and deletions.
checks: Compare returned source/hash against files in a controlled harness at request time.
Test same-size edits and restored mtimes, deletion, rename and project isolation.
Keep server assertions separate from independently observed freshness.
candidate_experiments.tradeoff: Hashing too much on every query raises local overhead; immutable snapshots, scoped checks and cached identities need adversarial tests.

candidate_experiments.mechanism: Prioritize exact symbol/path and relevant definitions, then a small dependency neighborhood; cap unrelated graph nodes.
checks: Use development retrieval fixtures for candidate ablations before freezing the new 40-task evaluation.
Report misses, complete-body/helper coverage, byte size and retrieval latency.
Do not tune to the final task grader after seeing its results.
candidate_experiments.tradeoff: Large helper closure wastes context; too narrow a closure misses aliases/callers or behavior across files.

candidate_experiments.mechanism: Stable tool names, schemas and field ordering; append changing task/source state after reusable metadata where the client permits.
checks: Record cached input as a subset of total input and derive uncached input explicitly.
Counterbalance arm ordering and disclose unresettable provider/OS caches.
Do not pad requests to manufacture cache hits.
candidate_experiments.tradeoff: Dynamic tool discovery can perturb prefix caching; no client-side guarantee of provider cache identity exists.

candidate_experiments.candidate: Cold and warm state as separate protocols
candidate_experiments.mechanism: Keep fresh-index A/B distinct from future related-task memory reuse.
checks: Freeze histories/memory content and split sessions without answer leakage.
Include indexing/setup time when incurred.
Report state/cache setup and unknown costs, including every failed attempt.
candidate_experiments.tradeoff: Warm memory may help related tasks but can introduce stale facts and leakage; a cold one-shot benchmark does not measure persistent memory value.

candidate_experiments.mechanism: Select structuredContent in generated code, or evaluate an explicit transport profile, after inspecting compatibility.
checks: Retain default MCP compatibility and structured semantics unless supported client testing justifies change.
Pilot on development tasks; compare actual native CLI usage and tool result parsing.
Keep the whole-envelope and selected-result hypotheses distinct.
candidate_experiments.tradeoff: Text-only results can impair typed consumers and yield no direct-mode token saving; native generated code is not fully observable through MCP events.

candidate_experiments.candidate: Frozen 40-task live comparison with honest accounting
candidate_experiments.mechanism: Use new tasks, isolated identical starting commits, stable prompts/model/settings, native structured usage, balanced order and independent behavioral grading.
checks: Freeze source, tasks and protocol before formal execution; do not discard pilot failures or rerun losers into the primary cohort.
Report every assigned/attempted run, failures, missing telemetry, paired cohorts, means/medians and sample counts.
Report actual cost per success only if complete reliable cost exists; otherwise null, never an estimate labeled actual.
candidate_experiments.tradeoff: Forty synthetic tasks cannot prove universal superiority; repeats and mirrored task families are not independent samples.

measurement_boundaries: No online example percentage is adopted as a Memglide performance claim.
No source here proves a universally best retriever or universal token/latency/cost saving.
Serialized source/context bytes, planning token budgets, completed CLI turns and MCP events are not exact model input tokens, model calls or filesystem I/O.
Actual cost and cost per success remain null without reliable complete cost telemetry.
Historical baseline remains immutable; new results must be written to new report paths.
